auto-b74c5eca632e.headline: Meloni urges EU to settle who negotiates on Ukraine
auto-b74c5eca632e.summary: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has criticised what she called a chaotic European approach to Ukraine talks, in a letter to European Council president Antonio Costa seen by AFP. She faulted the spread of parallel meetings, citing gatherings in Miami, Oslo and Brussels, and a call involving Norway, Finland and Vladimir Putin. Meloni asked EU leaders to decide who represents the bloc at the negotiating table, pointing to a Dublin summit and a December decision. Costa replied that the EU's role should be coherent and unified, and said he would raise the matter at the next leaders' meeting.

actors.why: Meloni pushes for clearer EU leadership but is not seeking a personal role
Internal disarray in talks risks irrelevance; leaders must now decide representation
Fragmented European diplomacy complicates efforts to secure a just end to the war
Washington revives its push and plans talks in Abu Dhabi with Russia and Ukraine
Trump touts a possible deal involving all of Europe, which Moscow could benefit from

impact_points: The European Union faces pressure to speak with one voice in Ukraine negotiations, or risk losing relevance.
Ukraine and its European partners are affected by fragmented talks while Washington pursues its own broader security arrangements with Russia.

auto-65cbd8aef227.headline: Turkish parliament approves defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
auto-65cbd8aef227.summary: Turkey's parliament has approved a defence agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, passing the bill 279 to 119 after a debate that continued from Wednesday into Thursday. The pact, signed in Mecca in August, includes a collective defence clause that mirrors Article 5 of the NATO treaty, so an attack on one member would bring assistance from the others. Saudi Arabia has faced recent strikes by Yemen's Houthis, and Turkish officials say their support would aim at deterrence rather than conflict with the Houthis. Critics have questioned whether Turkey's NATO commitments could conflict with the new pact, a concern Turkish officials have rejected.

actors.why: Parliament ratified a binding defence pact, adding obligations alongside NATO membership
Gains a collective defence partner amid escalating Houthi strikes on its territory
Joins a trilateral defence pact with Turkey and Saudi Arabia
Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia may face a deterrent from the new pact

impact_points: Turkey, a NATO member, takes on a new mutual defence obligation toward Saudi Arabia and Pakistan for ten years.
Saudi Arabia gains a potential security partner as Houthi attacks on its territory have escalated in recent months.

auto-c5c2fa63c83f.headline: Strikes on Taiz market reportedly leave dozens dead or hurt, per Houthi media
auto-c5c2fa63c83f.summary: Air strikes hit a market in Yemen's Taiz province on Friday morning, according to the Houthi-run Al-Masirah TV, which said more than 30 people were killed or wounded. The channel described the casualty figure as preliminary, with searches for missing people still under way and aircraft still overhead. Al-Masirah also reported strikes in Sanaa's Hamdan area, in Saada province's Majz district, and artillery and rocket fire near the Saudi border. The claims could not be independently verified from the reporting.

actors.why: Civilians reportedly killed or wounded in strikes on a market and other areas
Reported border fire and air activity could implicate Saudi forces in the strikes

impact_points: Yemen's Houthi authorities report heavy civilian casualties from strikes on a Taiz market, a serious humanitarian loss.
Saudi Arabia faces scrutiny as reported fire targets districts along the border, raising escalation concerns.

auto-27773f8c6f93.headline: Reported Russian missile launcher deal signals tightening Moscow-Tehran military ties
auto-27773f8c6f93.summary: The Financial Times reported that Russia agreed in 2024 to supply Iran with 90 advanced missile launchers, citing documents from a major Russian defence manufacturer. The launchers would carry Russia's LMUR precision missile and fit Mi-28 attack helicopters, which Iran already operates. Al Jazeera said it could not confirm whether the order had been delivered. The report followed a meeting between Vladimir Putin and Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei in Moscow, where they discussed regional security and the post-war period.

actors.why: Russia deepens ties with Iran but must avoid harming other relationships.
Iran gains advanced missile launchers and stronger Russian military backing.
Russian support for Iran during the US conflict with Iran adds pressure on Washington.
Russia's military ties to Iran sustain weapons use against Ukraine, indirectly.

impact_points: Iran gains a potential boost to its helicopter-based strike capability, strengthening its military position in the region.
Russia faces the balancing challenge of supporting Iran without damaging ties with Middle Eastern states and the United States.

auto-22b7d9e04eff.headline: Bahrain cracks down on Shi'ite clerics amid Iran war tensions
auto-22b7d9e04eff.summary: Bahraini authorities have arrested more than 50 Shi'ite clerics and religious speakers since May, accusing them of backing a group aiming to overthrow the government with Iranian help. Officials say Iran-linked ideology had spread in parts of the community after Iranian strikes on the island during the wider Iran war, which began in late February. Rights groups say 69 citizens of Iranian heritage have been stripped of citizenship and criticise the moves as a blow to free speech and religious freedom. A verdict in the clerics' case is expected on November 8, and the kingdom is preparing for possible protests.

actors.why: Government tightens control over clerics and faces possible protests and unrest.
Loses influence and diplomatic progress with Bahrain after the crackdown.

impact_points: Bahrain's Shi'ite community faces arrests, citizenship removals and fears of religious persecution.
Iran's influence in Bahrain is weakening, undoing recent steps toward restoring diplomatic relations.

auto-64506c5f5b2a.headline: Syria reportedly sends military advisers to help Saudi Arabia against Houthis
auto-64506c5f5b2a.summary: Two Syrian military sources and a senior US official say Damascus is providing Saudi Arabia with military advice and training as the kingdom faces Houthi attacks. Scores of personnel have reportedly travelled from Syria in recent weeks, and their mandate may be wider than advisory work. A Syrian diplomat called any deployment premature and said a Saudi-Syrian defence deal signed Wednesday covers advice, training and expertise exchange. A Saudi official said the cooperation mainly aims to restructure Syrian forces, and the Houthis and Saudi government did not respond to requests for comment.

actors.why: Gains Syrian training and advice against Houthi attacks on its territory
Deepens ties with Riyadh but risks entanglement in the regional war
Faces intensified Saudi-backed pressure in the renewed Yemen war
Urges Damascus to act cautiously to avoid wider regional escalation
Ratified a Mecca defence pact clearing the way for military support to Riyadh

impact_points: Saudi Arabia gains combat-tested Syrian expertise as it fights Houthi missile and drone attacks on its territory.
Syria risks being drawn into the wider regional war, which Washington has warned against, though Damascus publicly denies any deployment.

auto-a566b9c03bb0.headline: Greek-owned tanker attack kills sailor as Iran reports burning ships in Hormuz
auto-a566b9c03bb0.summary: A seafarer aboard a Greek-owned tanker was killed in an apparent missile strike in the Gulf, the company Velos Tankers said. The Marshall Islands-flagged vessel Velos Sapphire, travelling empty to Bahrain, was hit on Thursday and caught fire. Iranian state media and the Revolutionary Guards said several tankers were burning after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and blamed the American military for their route. The British maritime agency UKMTO reported a separate blast on a tanker off Oman, with its crew unharmed. The claims could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Greek-owned tanker attacked, crew member killed
Revolutionary Guards blame mines and claim tankers were violating routes
Accused by Iran of supporting tankers; mine-clearing and escort efforts face scrutiny
Vessel was sailing to Bahrain, a Gulf destination disrupted by the attacks
Tanker reported a blast at its waterline off Oman

impact_points: Greece and the Marshall Islands are affected, with a Greek-owned crew member killed and a flagged vessel damaged.
Gulf oil exports and global energy supply face risk as Hormuz traffic is disrupted by mines and attacks.

auto-759d950d654f.headline: Democratic midterm gains spark debate over future US Middle East policy
auto-759d950d654f.summary: Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress in the 3 November midterms, flipping several Republican-held Senate seats and making large House gains. Commentary in the article describes the result as a broad rejection of Donald Trump's presidency, citing economic concerns, the conflict with Iran, corruption charges and his use of presidential power. Exit polling reported that a majority of voters considered the decision to attack Iran wrong, and that concern over fuel prices was widespread. The piece questions whether the Democratic win will lead to a reassessment of US policy toward Israel, Palestine, Iran and the wider region, or a return to the old bipartisan consensus.

actors.why: Voters rejected the war and Trump's policies, opening a new Democratic congressional majority
Iran faces a US electorate that opposed the war and may pressure a policy change
Israel may face a rethink of unconditional US support as critics gain office
Palestinians may benefit if Washington reconsiders support for Israel's actions in Gaza

impact_points: Iran is affected by a US public that opposed the war and is reshaping Washington's approach.
Israel and Palestine face a possible shift in US policy as newly elected Democrats challenge long-held support for Israel.

auto-aecec173733d.headline: Umerov to head Ukrainian talks team in Abu Dhabi, official confirms
auto-aecec173733d.summary: Ukraine's foreign intelligence chief Rustem Umerov will lead Kyiv's negotiating team at trilateral talks with Russia and the United States in Abu Dhabi, scheduled for November 10. David Arakhamia, head of Zelensky's parliamentary group, confirmed this after reports had wrongly suggested Kyrylo Budanov would lead. Budanov has said these talks are not final and has tempered expectations of a breakthrough. European officials are not expected to attend, and EU leaders plan to discuss on November 13 how Europe should be represented.

actors.why: Kyiv continues negotiating with Moscow while pressing for a ceasefire and security guarantees.
Moscow attends talks despite rejecting a ceasefire and demanding Donbas.
Washington is reviving negotiations and hosting the trilateral format.
Europe is excluded from expected attendance despite funding Ukraine's defence.

impact_points: Ukraine is set to be represented by Umerov, with Kyiv seeking to raise recent Russian strikes at the talks.
Europe, which supplies most of Ukraine's military and financial aid, is not expected at the table, raising questions about its role in security guarantees.

auto-b179c1d25a35.headline: Trump hints at sweeping Ukraine deal after meeting Putin's envoy
auto-b179c1d25a35.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said he expects a major agreement on Ukraine that could extend to all of Europe, after meeting Kirill Dmitriev, the head of Russia's sanctioned sovereign wealth fund, at the White House on Thursday. Trump said he could not disclose what was discussed, though Russian and Ukrainian officials were also at an event that day where a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky was discussed. On Friday, Jared Kushner said Trump had raised the need for a broader European security framework with several European leaders. Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which began in February 2022, continues, and U.S.-brokered talks involving both sides are scheduled in Abu Dhabi for November 10-11.

actors.why: Ukraine's security future is under negotiation while Russian attacks continue
Russia may gain from talks involving its envoy and a possible deal
Washington is brokering talks and pursuing a wide agreement
European security architecture may be reshaped by a U.S.-backed framework

impact_points: Ukraine faces ongoing Russian bombardment while its future security arrangements are being negotiated over its head.
European states are being pulled into a possible U.S.-led security framework that could reshape the continent's defence arrangements.

auto-81ae2a85daa6.headline: US sanctions eight Canadian money firms accused of aiding Iran
auto-81ae2a85daa6.summary: The US Treasury has imposed sanctions on eight money services businesses based in Ontario and British Columbia, alleging they handled transactions for sanctioned Iranian entities. The measures cut the firms off from the dollar-based financial system, freezing any US-held assets and barring dealings with American people and companies. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Canada should not serve as a refuge for those helping Iran's government evade sanctions. Separately, the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network barred the offshore crypto exchange MEXC Global from US banking channels, citing alleged links to Iranian, North Korean and Russian sanctions evasion.

actors.why: Eight Canadian money firms are sanctioned and lose access to US financial system
Alleged sanctions-evasion channels through Canadian firms are being disrupted
Treasury extends pressure on Iran's financial channels beyond US borders
Crypto exchange MEXC Global, alleged to serve North Korean transactions, is cut off
MEXC Global is also cut off over alleged Russian sanctions-evasion transactions

impact_points: Canada faces scrutiny as eight of its money services firms are cut off from US finance.
Iran's money transfer channels abroad face further disruption as Washington widens its enforcement.

auto-8df97131c56e.headline: Democrats eye ending Trump's Canada tariffs after midterm wins
auto-8df97131c56e.summary: After Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, lawmakers are reportedly weighing legislation to roll back the 50% tariffs President Donald Trump imposed on some Canadian goods in August. Oregon Senator Ron Wyden, who is set to lead the Senate Finance Committee in January, said there is broad support for repeal and that discussions have begun. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has welcomed the push. Democrats may need some Republican votes to overcome a likely veto, and Trump allies doubt Congress can curb presidential tariff powers.

actors.why: Faces 50% tariffs on some goods; repeal would ease trade pressure
Congressional fight over presidential tariff powers and possible Republican split

impact_points: Canada stands to gain if Congress moves to repeal the 50% tariffs on some of its exports.
Lawmakers' ability to override Trump's tariff authority may be limited while he remains in office.

auto-0484b80cc361.headline: Iran weighs Qatari proposals on nuclear programme amid stalled US ceasefire talks
auto-0484b80cc361.summary:
Iran is reviewing a set of proposals from Qatar, the lead mediator, aimed at narrowing its differences with the United States over Tehran's nuclear activities, according to officials from both countries speaking anonymously. Tehran remains unwilling to enter negotiations on its nuclear programme until Washington accepts several core conditions tied to a ceasefire, the officials said. The White House declined to comment, while President Trump said discussions with Iran were ongoing.

The reported bridge plan would involve two days of trust-building steps: the US lifting its port blockade and releasing some frozen Iranian funds, with Iran granting inspectors access to bombed sites and reopening the Strait of Hormuz under an Iran-Oman arrangement not yet approved by Washington. Broader nuclear talks would follow.

actors.why: Reviewing mediated proposals but demanding blockade lifting, sanctions relief and compensation first
Under pressure from midterm losses and fuel prices, yet resisting Iran's core demands
Serving as chief mediator, gaining diplomatic standing in the talks
Its modified Strait of Hormuz agreement with Iran is central to the proposed deal
Israeli operations in Lebanon are among the regional hostilities Iran wants ended

impact_points: The United States faces pressure to accept Iranian conditions while its own midterm political position has weakened.
Iran and Qatar gain diplomatic leverage, while Oman's Strait of Hormuz arrangement and Gulf shipping stand to be affected.

auto-6974a4ab8de4.headline: Beijing condemns new US penalties targeting Chinese companies
auto-6974a4ab8de4.summary:
China has voiced strong objection to United States sanctions aimed at Chinese firms. Chinese officials argue the measures interfere in China's internal affairs and harm legitimate business. The report does not provide full details of the companies named or the precise scope of the penalties, so specifics could not be verified here.

Beijing's position signals a likely diplomatic response and continued friction over trade and technology restrictions between the two countries.

actors.why: Chinese firms face US penalties that Beijing publicly rejects
Sanctions on Chinese firms deepen tensions with Beijing

impact_points: China faces restrictions on its firms, which Beijing says damage legitimate commercial interests.
The United States faces a sharper diplomatic dispute with Beijing over its sanctions policy.

auto-cae9bfdc3d24.headline: US and Chinese trade officials hold call before Trump-Xi Shenzhen meeting
auto-cae9bfdc3d24.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer held a video call with Chinese Vice-Premier He Lifeng on Friday. The talks aimed to finalise preparations for a planned meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen later this month. According to a Treasury Department statement, Bessent urged Beijing to fully and quickly carry out commitments made in Busan and voiced concern about recent Chinese actions. He said further progress would depend on concrete results and that Washington would closely monitor implementation.

actors.why: Faces US pressure to implement Busan commitments and address concerns.
Pressing Beijing for results while preparing the summit with Xi.

impact_points: China faces US pressure to deliver on Busan commitments before the leaders' summit.
The United States is signalling it will judge trade progress by concrete results, shaping the Trump-Xi meeting.

auto-917a2ef46e7c.headline: Ukraine says strikes have crippled much of Russia's oil refining capacity
auto-917a2ef46e7c.summary: Ukrainian military intelligence says that by late September 2026, 15 of Russia's 38 main oil refineries were out of action and 12 more had cut output. Total refining at these plants fell 55.4% from the start of the year. The hardest-hit regions are the Volga, Central and Southern federal districts, where several major plants have stopped. Refineries in remote areas such as Omsk and Khabarovsk are still running and have partly offset shortages, though transport bottlenecks limit that. The intelligence service also claims the damage to Russia's oil sector exceeds $23.2 billion. These figures come from Ukraine's intelligence agency and could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Refining capacity collapsed, causing fuel shortages and forcing imports via grey schemes
Strikes on Russian oil infrastructure are presented as a key pressure tool

impact_points: Russia faces fuel shortages and struggles to meet domestic demand alongside its export commitments.
Russia reportedly imports fuel through grey schemes, and its refining losses could deepen into 2027 as maintenance is postponed.

auto-c00eab2541b1.headline: US-brokered Oleshky truce lets civilians leave; wider deal talk stalls
auto-c00eab2541b1.summary: Hundreds of residents of Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in Ukraine's Kherson region, were evacuated during a six-day ceasefire that Moscow and Kyiv both credited to Donald Trump. Melania Trump hosted Ukrainian and Russian delegates at the White House, where she called for a more lasting truce. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev also met Donald Trump, though the president declined to say what they discussed. A local government source told the BBC that evacuation work had begun about a year earlier and that others joined later and claimed credit.

actors.why: Civilians evacuated during truce, though the war continues and talks remain unsuccessful
Envoy met Trump and credited the US, but Oleshky remains Russian-occupied territory
Credited with brokering the truce and hosting delegations, but a wider deal has stalled

impact_points: Ukraine and Russia gain a humanitarian pause, with Oleshky civilians escaping starvation and bombardment during the truce.
The US and its leaders take a visible role, though Moscow and Kyiv have not detailed the extent of Melania Trump's involvement.

auto-7f443b0f0ea5.headline: North Korea's state-trained hackers linked to massive Binance crypto theft
auto-7f443b0f0ea5.summary: A Rappler report says North Korea has built a large, state-backed hacking force that recruits talented children early and rewards successful operatives with housing, cash shares of heist proceeds and party membership. The piece cites defectors and analysts, including a former trainer who fled to South Korea in 2004, and describes a program that selects about 150 to 200 students a year. It also says the group was behind the $6.3 billion Binance hack. The FBI and Binance have blamed North Korea, while Pyongyang denies involvement. South Korean intelligence estimated about 8,400 people work in the North's cyber operations.

actors.why: Hacking heists generate hard currency and strategic cyber capability for the regime
South Korean intelligence tracks the threat and defectors have fled there
FBI attributes the Binance hack to North Korea, raising security concerns

impact_points: North Korea benefits from crypto heists that fund the regime and its weapons programmes through hard currency.
Binance and the crypto sector face losses and growing security risks from state-backed hacking groups.

auto-8c71b14b22db.headline: Washington presses Beijing to deliver on rare earths and farm purchase pledges
auto-8c71b14b22db.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer met Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng to press Beijing to carry out its commitments under the Busan trade agreement without delay. The US Treasury said continued progress depends on tangible results and that Washington will closely monitor implementation, also voicing concern over recent Chinese actions. China's commerce ministry responded that it is willing to buy more American farm products, but only if both sides put in place the agreed reciprocal tariff reduction of $30 billion each.

actors.why: Washington presses Beijing and seeks farm sales and tariff relief
Beijing is pressed to act but conditions farm purchases on reciprocal cuts

impact_points: China faces US pressure to implement the Busan deal, including tariff cuts and tech restrictions relief.
US farmers and exporters could gain if Beijing expands agricultural purchases, while the trade truce stays fragile.

auto-bbf7944dae2e.headline: Saudi coalition says it downed Houthi missile aimed at Medina region
auto-bbf7944dae2e.summary: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said its air defences intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile that the Houthis fired toward Medina. Saudi civil defence had issued a warning about possible danger near the port of Yanbu shortly before, and later said the threat had passed. The Houthis denied targeting the city, saying their attacks hit only oil facilities and military bases. Yanbu, a key oil export hub linked to the East-West pipeline, has been targeted by the Houthis several times recently. Separately, Yemeni government forces claimed gains in Taiz, which Al Jazeera could not independently verify.

actors.why: Missile attacks threaten Yanbu oil exports and disrupt airports and air traffic
Houthi missile fire and government offensive continue fighting across Yemen
Iran-aligned Houthis keep pressuring Saudi Arabia amid the wider regional war

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces ongoing missile threats that could disrupt oil exports through Yanbu and air traffic.
Global oil markets depend on Yanbu's shipments, so any further attacks could affect supply to international buyers.

auto-82c9b6fff018.headline: Iran says its forces are stronger and on higher alert after war
auto-82c9b6fff018.summary: An Iranian army spokesman, Mohammad Akraminia, says the country's armed forces are stronger and more motivated than when the war with the United States and Israel began in February. He said the military has gained experience from direct confrontation and now has greater commitment and self-confidence. Akraminia also claimed Iran still controls the Strait of Hormuz and will keep it closed until Washington accepts Tehran's demands. He added that any military response, under the Supreme Leader's orders, would be immediate and not limited geographically. The statements were carried by the state news agency Irna and were not independently verified.

actors.why: Military signals readiness; keeps Hormuz closed as leverage in standoff
Iran demands its acceptance while Hormuz remains shut and threats continue
Named as wartime adversary facing an Iranian warning of immediate response

impact_points: Iran faces continued pressure and risk of renewed fighting, as its military signals readiness to respond without limits.
The United States and Israel face heightened threat, with Tehran maintaining the Strait of Hormuz closure as leverage in its demands.

auto-a07030a3fef5.headline: Trump says recent calls on ending Ukraine war, more talks planned
auto-a07030a3fef5.summary: US President Donald Trump told reporters he has held phone calls aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, and that further calls and meetings are scheduled for the coming days. He argued that Ukraine and Russia are now willing to negotiate for the first time. Trump did not name the people he spoke with, and he again described a potential deal as a major settlement. The remarks offer no details on terms or on whether either side has agreed to a framework.

actors.why: Possible path to ending war, but no terms or commitments announced yet
Named as a party ready to negotiate, with no concessions reported
Trump is actively pushing calls and meetings to broker a settlement

impact_points: Ukraine could see a diplomatic opening toward ending the fighting, though no terms have been disclosed.
Russia is also drawn into the talks Trump described, with its position on any settlement still unclear from his remarks.

auto-c470e4bc601b.headline: Russian ballistic missile barrages strike Kyiv overnight, injuring several and damaging a bridge
auto-c470e4bc601b.summary: Overnight on November 6-7, several waves of Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv, hours after President Zelensky warned of a further large-scale strike on infrastructure. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said at least five people in the city were wounded, including a 14-year-old girl, and two were hospitalised. The Northern Bridge was damaged and closed to traffic in both directions, and a residential building, a non-residential building and a kindergarten were reportedly hit. In the Brovary district of the surrounding region, a drone attack set a home on fire and injured one man. The full extent of the damage was not yet clear when the report was published.

actors.why: Missile and drone strikes injured residents and damaged the Northern Bridge and homes.
Launched the missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and the surrounding region.

impact_points: Ukraine, and Kyiv's roughly three million residents, face fresh casualties and damage to transport and civilian sites.
Kyiv's energy and water supply, already strained by recent strikes ahead of winter, faces further pressure.

auto-dd84a0ad71db.headline: Russian missile strike hits Kyiv, two people hurt, ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
auto-dd84a0ad71db.summary:
Russian forces fired ballistic missiles at Kyiv on Saturday, according to the city's mayor, Vitali Klitschko. Debris damaged a five-storey apartment block in a western district and another residential building, and two people were injured. A kindergarten building was also hit, the city's military administration said. The attack came after President Zelenskyy warned that Moscow was preparing strikes on energy, bridges and other infrastructure. It also came days before planned US-led Ukrainian-Russian talks in Abu Dhabi.

The article also covers wider context: Brussels talks among Western allies on post-war security and reconstruction, and a deadly strike on an aid point in Zaporizhia's Komyshuvakha that Ukraine says killed 50 people.

actors.why: Kyiv hit, civilians injured, and infrastructure threatened by missile strikes
Ordered strikes while peace talks with the US are set to open

Allies in Brussels backing Ukraine's security guarantees and reconstruction

impact_points: Ukraine faces fresh civilian harm and infrastructure damage in Kyiv as strikes continue before peace talks.
Russia's position in the planned Abu Dhabi talks and its standing with Washington are shaped by this escalation and Trump's remarks on a possible deal.

auto-676a0a3ddc2e.headline: French unions and Yellow Vests plan rival Paris rallies amid cost-of-living unrest
auto-676a0a3ddc2e.summary: French unions and student groups are holding another day of protests on Saturday, with an authorised march in central Paris. A separate Yellow Vests rally at Place de la Concorde goes ahead despite an authorities' ban, and the movement has called for mass disobedience. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said 70,000 security personnel would be deployed nationwide. Earlier protests were largely peaceful but included clashes and vandalism, including the worst rioting in years on October 17. Protesters demand a higher minimum wage, wage rises, tax reform and better learning conditions for young people, with less than six months before the presidential election.

actors.why: Nationwide protests and strikes pressure the government over wages and costs.
France's debt pressures and unrest are watched within the bloc's second-largest economy.

impact_points: France faces a tense security operation and pressure from protesters over wages and living costs.
The government has limited room to meet demands because the economy is under strain to reduce debt.

auto-ef36570cbd07.headline: Overnight Russian strikes hit Kyiv region, injuring five and damaging a bridge
auto-ef36570cbd07.summary: Russian attacks overnight damaged energy facilities and a bridge in the Kyiv region and in neighbouring Zhytomyr, according to Ukrainian authorities. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said heating and water supplies in the capital were disrupted and the situation was extremely difficult. The Pivnichnyi Bridge was closed in both directions for structural checks, and five people, including a child, were wounded. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned of more strikes on energy and civilian infrastructure and again urged faster delivery of Patriot interceptors, which he said could take years despite a US approval of a $2.1 billion package.

actors.why: Energy, bridge and civilian infrastructure damaged; five wounded in the capital
Its strikes on Ukrainian energy and civilian infrastructure continue
Approved a $2.1 billion Patriot package, though delivery timing remains uncertain

Ukraine's air defences remain exposed while Patriot interceptor deliveries from allies are delayed.

auto-2fb43e7f9be8.headline: Qatar proposes Hormuz reopening linked to nuclear inspections in Iran
auto-2fb43e7f9be8.summary:
Qatar, mediating between the United States and Iran, is pressing Tehran to let UN nuclear inspectors visit bombed nuclear sites, including those holding highly enriched uranium. Under the proposal, the US would lift its naval blockade and release part of about $8bn in frozen Iranian assets, while Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the second day of implementation via a route agreed with Oman. Iran has also set further conditions, including an end to the Lebanon war and reparations, and has voiced distrust of the IAEA's head, Rafael Grossi.

Reports also say Iran has allowed ships from China, India, Qatar and Iraq through the strait, with differing fee arrangements, and that the IRGC said two tankers struck mines after using an unauthorised route.

actors.why: Could reopen the strait and gain frozen assets, but faces inspection and sanctions demands
Would lift naval blockade and release funds, but Trump still weighs new strikes on nuclear sites
Acts as lead mediator, boosting its diplomatic role in the conflict
Co-manages the agreed shipping route and proposes a long-term strait administration

impact_points: Iran would regain shipping access and frozen funds if the deal proceeds, but must accept inspections and other concessions.
China and India, which take large shares of Gulf crude passing through Hormuz, would be affected by any reopening of the strait.

auto-a1d870f91e9e.headline: Iran says Hormuz stays closed until US accepts its seven conditions
auto-a1d870f91e9e.summary: Iran's army spokesman, Brigadier General Mohammad Akraminia, said the Strait of Hormuz will only reopen if Washington accepts Iran's seven conditions, which he described as the sole route to reopening. He warned that renewed aggression or provocations in the region would not lead to the waterway reopening. He also relayed directives from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei calling for swift, effective responses to any attack, with no geographical limits, meaning US assets anywhere could be treated as potential targets. The statements were made by Iranian officials and were not independently verified.

impact_points: The United States is affected because Iran says it must accept seven conditions before the strait reopens.
Iran is pressing its demands while threatening a response to US forces beyond West Asia, raising regional tension for Gulf shipping and neighbours.

auto-5a6f9316ef13.headline: Merz and Hungary's Magyar to meet in Berlin on Ukraine and EU matters
auto-5a6f9316ef13.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is set to host Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar at the Federal Chancellery in Berlin on 10 November, with talks starting at 11:00. According to the German government's press service, the agenda covers European affairs, defence, economic cooperation and ongoing support for Ukraine, including a working lunch with selected ministers. The meeting follows a phone call Merz held with US President Donald Trump on 5 November about Russia's war against Ukraine.

auto-4be8aa3fb9e8.headline: Winter storms flood Gaza camps and endanger damaged buildings
auto-4be8aa3fb9e8.summary: Heavy rain and strong winds have flooded tent camps and damaged structures across Gaza, with water levels rising 30 to 40 centimetres at several camps after a recent storm. Families in al-Mina camp in the north, where about 1,700 households live, say rainwater soaked their bedding and clothing, and one family's tent collapsed. In Nuseirat, central Gaza, a resident living in a tower block hit by an Israeli strike in September 2025 says his apartment is unsafe, with debris still falling from upper floors. The UN's OCHA estimates about 950,000 displaced people live in flood-exposed areas.

Israeli bombardments caused the building damage that now leaves residents at risk

impact_points: Displaced Palestinian families in Gaza face flooding, cold and unsafe shelter as winter arrives.
Gaza's municipality is overwhelmed, with much of its drainage and sewage network damaged and limited capacity to cope.

auto-86de3cc4b51f.headline: Russian strikes leave Kyiv short of power and water ahead of peace talks
auto-86de3cc4b51f.summary: Russia launched a large overnight attack on Kyiv and surrounding regions, using 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles against electricity substations and a bridge over the Dnipro River. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes aimed to plunge the capital and the country into darkness, leaving residents facing power, water and heat problems; five people were injured, including a 14-year-old girl. Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the US are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday. Russia's defence ministry said the strikes targeted energy and transport sites.

actors.why: Kyiv's power, water and heat supplies hit by missile and drone strikes

Kyiv appeals for more support; US-led talks seek a deal to end the war
European partners are sceptical of Russia-linked security proposals for Europe

impact_points: Ukraine's capital Kyiv faces prolonged blackouts and water shortages as winter approaches, with civilians bearing the strain.
Ukraine and its European partners are wary of a US-backed framework that Moscow may use to press its demands on Nato.

auto-a0df2c378e3a.headline: Iraq warns against being drawn into renewed US-Iran conflict
auto-a0df2c378e3a.summary:
Iraq's prime minister, Ali al-Zaidi, spoke with US President Donald Trump by phone, pressing that Iraqi territory must not be used for attacks on neighbouring states. His foreign minister, Fuad Hussein, said a fresh war with Iran would be disastrous for Iraq and that the country is not ready for conflict. Iraq has already suffered heavy losses, with reported oil revenue losses above $60bn since the war began and its exports largely disrupted by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

The remarks come as diplomatic efforts intensify to prevent renewed US attacks on Iran. Baghdad has been trying to balance its ties with Washington and Tehran while pursuing the disarmament of pro-Iran armed groups.

Diplomatic pressure to avert US strikes while Iraq seeks neutrality

impact_points: Iraq faces heavy economic strain from lost oil revenue and disrupted exports through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iraq risks being dragged into a renewed conflict through attacks from armed groups and both the US and Iran.

auto-0eb32678ae60.headline: Trump names Stephen Miller chief of staff despite midterm rebuke on immigration
auto-0eb32678ae60.summary: President Donald Trump has appointed Stephen Miller, the architect of his aggressive immigration policies, as White House chief of staff. The move came days after voters in the US midterm elections rejected Republican candidates across the country, including on Trump's mass deportation campaign. Critics say the appointment signals faster deportations and tougher enforcement, and Democrats in Congress are preparing to scrutinise Miller's role through oversight and investigations.

actors.why: Trump's immigration agenda is set to intensify under Miller's leadership, drawing congressional scrutiny.

impact_points: Undocumented immigrants and asylum seekers in the US face expected acceleration of deportations and enforcement raids.
Democrats who regained control of parts of Congress plan oversight and investigations, setting up a clash with the White House.

auto-5ac89fafa1c6.headline: Trump expected to meet Xi in Shenzhen after Republican midterm losses
auto-5ac89fafa1c6.summary: After Republicans lost control of both chambers of the US Congress in midterm elections, US President Donald Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in about two weeks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders' meeting in Shenzhen. The article notes that China hosted Barack Obama at a G20 summit in Hangzhou a decade earlier, when he was similarly weakened politically. If the meeting goes ahead, it would be the two leaders' third in-person encounter this year. The piece frames the Apec gathering as a test of whether Trump can reach lasting agreements with Beijing.

impact_points: China is preparing to host a US leader whose domestic political standing has weakened after the midterms.
US-China relations could shift depending on whether the Shenzhen talks produce durable agreements.

auto-01f008da18f1.headline: US strikes hit Qeshm as Hormuz shipping attacks and mediation efforts continue
auto-01f008da18f1.summary:
The United States struck Iran's Qeshm island after vessels were targeted in the Strait of Hormuz, while mediators work to stop a wider clash. Two projectiles reportedly hit the island on Friday night, part of a series of strikes on Iranian air defences and launchers in recent weeks. Iran's army said it downed a US MQ-9 drone, and the Revolutionary Guard claimed an MQ-1 interception. UKMTO reported at least 11 ships attacked around the strait in the week to November 6, with shipping traffic about 65 percent below pre-conflict levels.

Iran's Revolutionary Guard said limits on its missile range no longer apply, and Iran's foreign minister said he had held talks with 12 foreign ministers, including those of Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

impact_points: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen sharply, hurting global oil flows and regional trade routes.

auto-765b4160a9be.headline: Italian foreign minister says personal data posted by suspected pro-Russian hackers
auto-765b4160a9be.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said his personal information was published on the dark web by hackers he described as pro-Russian, and he linked the move to Rome's backing for Ukraine. He said the group sought more details about him and his family and offered to pay for them. Screenshots reviewed by Reuters showed his photo on a list of 18 people labelled hostile to Russia, which also included cybersecurity experts. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed support for Tajani and called the sale of officials' confidential data a serious concern. Moscow has not responded, and Russia has consistently denied involvement in hacking abroad.

auto-1003cf144b18.headline: Qatar's prime minister says Washington open to ending conflict with Iran
auto-1003cf144b18.summary: Qatar's prime minister has said the United States is prepared to look for a way to bring its war with Iran to an end. auto-41c5fd51895e.headline: Trump confirms US strikes on Iranian air defences near Qeshm Island
auto-41c5fd51895e.summary: US President Donald Trump has acknowledged American strikes on Iranian air defence systems on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, describing them as minor and brief. Iranian state media reported missile strikes in the Suza area and said Iranian forces shot down an American MQ-9 drone over the island. US Central Command described the situation as relatively calm and declined further comment. Trump also said Washington is in talks with Tehran and has made significant progress, without giving details. Qatar, which is mediating, rejected reports that negotiations had collapsed.

auto-d162e8e13201.headline: Beijing hosts seventh high-level media dialogue during World Media Summit
auto-d162e8e13201.summary: The seventh high-level dialogue of the World Media Summit took place in Beijing, bringing together media representatives for discussion on the sector's direction. auto-24fe872cac9b.headline: Ukraine says Russia fired North Korean missiles in overnight attack
auto-24fe872cac9b.summary: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said Russian forces used North Korean-made KN-23 ballistic missiles in a large overnight strike on 6-7 November that hit a key energy facility. Of 36 missiles launched on a ballistic trajectory, he said only four were intercepted. Forensic examinations are still under way at the impact sites. Substations in several oblasts, including Vinnytsia, Zhytomyr, Rivne, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk, were damaged, and 12 regions beyond Kyiv were attacked. Nine people were injured, one of them a child.

auto-c4cb6519b181.summary: Iran has said it no longer observes a voluntary restriction it had placed on how far its missiles can travel. auto-b75e562b7c70.headline: Iraq's foreign minister says outside actors are using Iraqi territory for attacks
auto-b75e562b7c70.summary:
Iraq's foreign minister, Fuad Hussein, told Al Jazeera that Baghdad holds evidence that outside parties have used Iraqi territory to launch strikes on neighbouring states. Baghdad is probing attacks aimed at Gulf countries and is pursuing talks with Saudi Arabia over the dispute. Saudi Arabia has blamed Iran-aligned groups in Iraq for attacks on its oil infrastructure, and Iraq confirmed in September that drones hitting a Saudi pipeline came from Iraqi soil.

Hussein also said Iraq is negotiating with Iran-aligned factions to place their weapons under state control, and that Washington has asked for most border crossings with Iran to close. He added that Iraq lost about $60bn when Strait of Hormuz oil shipments were halted, and that shipments have resumed under understandings with the US and Iran.

auto-bc6eb4d49cdf.headline: Ukraine names Russian officers and pilots over deadly Komyshuvakha shelter strike
auto-bc6eb4d49cdf.summary: Ukraine's military intelligence says it has identified Russian personnel it believes were involved in a November 2 airstrike on an underground school in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, where civilians were collecting aid. Local authorities put the death toll at no fewer than 55, with more than 50 others still missing and rescue work continuing for days. HUR named a Russian officer it says planned the attack, along with six pilots of Su-34 fighter-bombers, and said a seventh crew was still being identified. President Zelensky called for stronger air defence support from partners.
